---
title: "Quiz: Welch t-test"
---

[Exercises](17-welch-test.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/17-welch-test/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** Which study matches the independent groups used in this lesson?

(i) The same plants measured before and after treatment.  

(ii) Separate plants randomly allocated to treated and control groups.  

(iii) Several leaves taken from one plant in each group.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Identify the unit that received treatment independently.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). The independent unit is a plant. Measurements on the same plant are
related; many leaves from one plant do not supply many independently treated
plants.
:::

---

**Q2.** Mean growth is 21.49 mm in treated plants and 15.28 mm in controls.
What difference does `t.test(treated, control)` estimate, and in what units?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Subtract the second group's mean from the first group's mean.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Treated minus control: $21.49 - 15.28 = 6.21$ mm using the rounded means.
The difference from the full data is about 6.22 mm.
:::

---

**Q3.** A treated-minus-control 95% confidence interval is [2.70, 9.73] mm.
What interval and two-sided p-value would result from reversing the vector order?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Negate both endpoints, then put the lower endpoint first. The equal-means
question is the same in either direction.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The interval is [−9.73, −2.70] mm. The two-sided p-value is unchanged.
:::

---

**Q4.** Which statement correctly interprets a 95% confidence interval for a
mean difference?

(i) It contains 95% of individual plants' growth values.  

(ii) Its procedure covers the true mean difference in about 95% of repeated
experiments under the assumptions.  

(iii) Every value inside it has the same probability of being the true difference.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The interval describes uncertainty in a population mean difference.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). The coverage statement concerns repeated use of the procedure. The interval
is not an individual-growth range, and it does not give equally probable values
of the fixed population difference.
:::

---

**Q5.** The p-value is 0.0015. Does this mean there is a 0.15% probability that
the treatment has no effect? What does the p-value describe?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Begin with “If the equal-means model and its assumptions held …”.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
No. If the equal-means model and assumptions held, a two-sided t statistic at
least this extreme would occur with probability about 0.0015. The p-value does
not assign a probability to the hypothesis or measure biological importance.
:::

---

**Q6.** For the same observations, will a 99% confidence interval be wider or
narrower than the 95% interval? Will the group means change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A higher coverage target requires more room around the same estimate.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Wider. The observed group means stay the same; only the interval level changes.
:::
